title: Florida House, District 38
what_it_does: Represents District 38 in the Florida House of Representatives; votes on state laws and the state budget.
decided_note: Open seat: Republican Rep. David Smith is term-limited. Republicans Emily Duda Buckley and Marcus Hyatt met in the Aug. 18 Republican primary; the winner faces Democrat Michelle DeJesus on Nov. 3. The primary result could not be verified.
verified_ballot_note: Oviedo Community News (June 17, 2026) reported the HD 38 field: Republicans Emily Duda Buckley (of Duda Farm Fresh Foods, Oviedo) and Marcus Hyatt in the primary, with the winner facing Democrat Michelle DeJesus in November (https://oviedocommunitynews.org/2026/06/17/whos-on-the-seminole-county-primary-ballot-for-2026/). The Aug. 18 primary winner was not found in search snippets; both Republicans are listed below pending verification. Research limitation: every WebFetch (Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, Division of Elections, county SOEs, news sites) was blocked and the search budget was capped, so this roster comes only from search-result snippets and should be re-verified against the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: Emily Duda Buckley
candidates.occupation: Duda Farm Fresh Foods family; foster and adoptive parent; Guardian ad Litem
candidates.background: Republican candidate for HD 38 associated with Duda Farm Fresh Foods Inc. in Oviedo; ran in the Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary against Marcus Hyatt (result unverified).

taxes.summary: Describes herself as a free-market conservative who would lower costs by reducing taxes and regulations, and says government should live within its means.
taxes.quote: As a free-market conservative, I firmly believe we can fuel prosperity and lower costs for families by empowering job creators, reducing taxes, and eliminating burdensome regulations.

sources.title: Florida Chamber of Commerce endorsement release
Emily Duda Buckley for Florida House - Home

property_tax.summary: Pledges to cut property taxes so families and seniors can stay in their communities; does not call for eliminating them.
property_tax.quote: cut property taxes so families and seniors can afford to stay in the communities they built

sources.title: Emily Duda Buckley for Florida House - Home

insurance.summary: On property insurance Duda Buckley said she supports building on recent reforms that she said reduced fraud and litigation, encouraging more carriers to compete in Florida, and strengthening mitigation programs such as My Safe Florida Home so homeowners can earn lower rates.
insurance.quote: I support building on the recent reforms that reduced fraud and frivolous litigation, encouraging more carriers to compete here

sources.title: Emily Duda Buckley — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

housing.summary: Duda Buckley said affordability comes down to expanding supply and lowering government-added costs. She said she would build on the Live Local Act by streamlining and digitizing permitting with deadlines and automatic approvals, opening zoning tools such as accessory dwelling units, expanding employer-sponsored workforce housing and down-payment assistance, and reducing impact fees and regulatory costs.
housing.quote: Affordability comes down to two things: expanding supply and lowering the costs government adds.

sources.title: Emily Duda Buckley — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

immigration.summary: Duda Buckley said she supports enforcing immigration laws, securing the border and state-federal cooperation, while adding that Florida's farms, small businesses and hospitality employers depend on a reliable legal workforce and that enforcement should be paired with improvements to guest-worker and visa programs.
immigration.quote: I support enforcing our immigration laws, securing the border, and the cooperation between state and federal authorities that keeps our communities safe

sources.title: Emily Duda Buckley — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

abortion.summary: In the Oviedo Community News general-election questionnaire (Sept. 30, 2026) Duda Buckley said she supports Florida's current abortion law and believes it should stay the same, describing the existing limit with exceptions for rape, incest and the life of the mother as a reasonable balance.
abortion.quote: I support Florida's current law and believe it should stay the same.

candidates.name: Nik Dean
candidates.background: Nikolas 'Nik' Dean, a Seminole County attorney, was chosen by Democratic leaders on Aug. 31, 2026 to replace Michelle DeJesus, who withdrew, as the Democratic nominee for HD 38 (Florida Democratic Party release; Florida Politics). His launch statement focuses on lowering everyday costs, raising wages and safety; no issue-by-issue positions were published as of Sept. 18, 2026.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

insurance.summary: In the Oviedo Community News general-election questionnaire (Sept. 30, 2026) Dean named home ownership and property insurance as a top problem and said the cost of property insurance should be reduced by capping how much insurers can raise premiums.
insurance.quote: We also need to decrease the cost of property insurance by capping the amount property insurers can increase premiums.

sources.title: Nik Dean — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile
Voter Guide – General Election 2026 (Oviedo Community News)

housing.summary: Dean said the supply of affordable housing should be increased through what he called smart development, including building new affordable housing and retrofitting underutilized properties, while protecting the county's character and ecosystem.
housing.quote: We need to increase the supply of affordable housing through smart development, which includes building new affordable housing solutions and retrofitting underutilized properties.

sources.title: Nik Dean — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

healthcare.summary: Dean said he would work to expand access to health care and child care through tax incentives for employers that offer comprehensive benefits and would add accountability and transparency to medication pricing so insurers cannot block access to care.
healthcare.quote: No one should have to choose between groceries and medicine.

sources.title: Nik Dean — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

property_tax.summary: Dean said he will vote No on Amendment 3, saying Floridians need relief but not at the cost of cutting funding for first responders, libraries and police, and that the benefits for homeowners would not reach renters or business owners.
property_tax.quote: I will vote NO. Floridians need relief, but not at the cost of slashing funding to resources like our first responders, libraries and police force.

sources.title: Nik Dean — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

environment.summary: Asked to name the biggest environmental issue in his district, Dean said the destruction of Seminole County's wetlands, saying prioritizing rapid development over wetland preservation increases flood risk and depletes the aquifer.
environment.quote: Development must be executed with an intention to protect Florida's ecosystem.

sources.title: Nik Dean — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

immigration.summary: Dean said the federal government should deport undocumented immigrants with a history of violent crime and that borders should be secure, but that there must also be a clear pathway to citizenship for other immigrants, and that state funds should not be used to build or run immigration detention facilities.
immigration.quote: we should not utilize state funds to create and run immigration detention facilities

sources.title: Nik Dean — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

abortion.summary: Dean said he supports amending Florida's constitution to codify abortion rights comparable to those under Roe v. Wade and supports a woman's right to choose.
abortion.quote: I support an amendment to Florida's constitution codifying abortion rights akin to those previously afforded under Roe.

sources.title: Nik Dean — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

growth.summary: Dean said he does not support state preemption as a general principle because local issues require local solutions, and that he would vote to protect Seminole County's voter-approved rural boundary, describing a communal approach to development as necessary.
growth.quote: the government's role is to serve the interests of their constituents, not the interests of a few developers

sources.title: Nik Dean — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

energy.summary: On rising utility costs and data centers, Dean said AI companies should not socialize the cost of added water and energy demand while privatizing the profits, and that legislators should ensure data centers rather than Floridians carry those costs.
energy.quote: AI companies cannot socialize the rising costs of utilities and privatize the profits of the data centers creating these rising costs.

sources.title: Nik Dean — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

other_issues.summary: Says hard work alone is not enough when groceries, gas, housing, health care and insurance outpace wages, and pledges practical solutions that lower everyday costs and raise wages.
other_issues.quote: Hard work alone is not enough when costs of everyday items like groceries, gas, housing, healthcare, and insurance continue to outpace the workers in our state's wages.

sources.title: Nik Dean launches campaign for House District 38 - Florida Democratic Party

other_issues.title: Affordability
other_issues.summary: In his qualifying announcement Dean said his campaign is focused on the state's affordability crisis and on lowering the cost of groceries, gas, housing, health care and insurance for Seminole County families and seniors; he said he would 'hit the ground running, meet voters where they are, and hear their concerns about the real issues.'

sources.title: Democrat Nik Dean Officially Qualifies for House District 38 Race (The Floridian)

other_issues.title: Cost of living
other_issues.summary: Dean says he is running because of what he calls the state's affordability crisis, arguing that wages are not keeping up with everyday costs, and that he would focus on lowering costs, raising wages and making communities safe and affordable. He has not published detailed positions on individual bills.
